nodes.label: Per-Method Wall-Clock Timeout (180s default)
nodes.rationale: Heavy methods (SPPR_EwE path enumeration, Monte-Carlo drivers) can run for hours and cannot be interrupted once inside numpy/sympy, so each method runs in a worker process with a wall-clock budget; an overrun is killed, recorded as a timeout (not a failure) in run_notes' status column, and the export moves on to the next method. One shared worker keeps the cost to a single process spawn per directory rather than per model.

nodes.label: Group-Level Jensen-Affected PPR Aggregation (SeaAroundUs)
nodes.rationale: Commercial/functional group SPPR exponentiates the group's catch-weighted mean trophic level once, rather than summing each taxon's own exponentiated SPPR. Because SPPR = 10^(TL-1) is convex, this is a direct, deliberate application of Jensen's inequality: group PPR can only ever be ≤ the sum of its member taxa's PPR, never more. The gap is kept on purpose — it measures the cost of moving from taxa to groups, which an Ecopath model cannot show on its own because it has no taxon level. In this 2019 EEZ release the understatement is 22.27% for commercial groups and 14.44% for functional groups; the top-level repository README reports a related but distinct 'globally' measured figure of 22.93%/16.48%.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 Table S3 diet matrix
nodes.rationale: Table S3 C3:Y27 has 25 prey rows and 23 consumers. All 575 slots, including 232 numeric cells, were verified. Consumer sums range 0.9996-1.0005 and source blanks remain blank. Source CSV and model.json are not normalised; the converter normalises ten columns by at most 0.05%.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 unknown biomass accumulation
nodes.rationale: No numeric annual BA or migration is supplied. BA remains blank/-9999; across-century state change is not annual BA. Turbot and Ling reconciliation may reflect rounded B but adjusted values were not adopted.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 indeterminate mass balance
nodes.rationale: With EE tolerance 0.05, the checker reports 0 errors, 2 indeterminate groups, 3 warnings and 2 notes. BA is unknown in all 25 groups, so recomputation without BA does not establish steady state. Turbot printed EE 0.82 versus computed 0.991; Ling computed EE 1.003.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 endotherm P/Q warnings
nodes.rationale: Seabirds P/Q 0.006, Seals 0.004 and Cetaceans 0.002 lie below the usual 0.02-0.5 range. Published rounded values were retained; these are not evidence of a shifted table column.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 loader transformations
nodes.rationale: The converter defaults habitat area to 1, normalises ten diet columns, zeros absent diet links/fates and leaves GS/BA unknown. The SPPR loader applies GS 0.2 except Small zooplankton 0.4, fills the detritus destination and solves BA during balancing. groups_df is a transformed computational model, not author measurements; LOADER_TRANSFORMATIONS.csv preserves provenance. Cross-model interpretation: Source-preserving metadata updates and numerical loader transformations both require separating author input from computational output.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 deliberate source blanks
nodes.rationale: GS, BA, migration, detritus routing/import and habitat fractions lack source measurements. Inapplicable QB/PB/PQ fields blank. Authors excluded discards, not measured them at zero. No source import diet row supplied.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 configuration-specific method health
nodes.rationale: GE and With Egestion are OK. The default repaired-EE TE configuration fails with living spectral radius 1.11278. Finite output does not prove convergence. GE is the diagnostic reference; explicitly failed configurations and negative source-group SPPR are excluded. The diagnostic does not grade every TE-named solver or the Monte Carlo accepted-draw subset. Cross-model interpretation: Computational completion and taxonomic coverage cannot validate a configuration with failed convergence.

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 unidentified demersal inference

nodes.label: EastCoastScotland1991-1995 validation results

Mapping covers 384 taxa with 14 composites and 62 unresolved: 99.597% tonnage mapped, 81.2% source-confirmed, 15.9% low confidence. nodes.label: Karnataka2000 source membership precedence
nodes.rationale: All 129 numbered CMFRI members were transcribed from printed pp.11-12/PDF pp.21-22. Exact model strings Skates & Rays and Micro Nekton remain. The source puts Thryssa in Clupeids, Bregmaceros in Anchovies, jellyfish in Micro Nekton, Plotosus/Fistularia in Benthic Omnivores, Parastromateus in Med Benthic Carnivores, and ponyfishes/Lactarius in Small Benthic Carnivores. nodes.label: Karnataka2000 independent mapping re-derivation
nodes.rationale: No inherited_mapping row remains. Prior assignments were not inputs to new membership, definition and inference rules. 101 group expressions changed and previous notes were archived as superseded history. This is re-derivation, not blinded independent-agent testing.

nodes.label: Karnataka2000 limited nomenclature aliases
nodes.rationale: Formio niger was reconciled with Parastromateus niger and Loligo/Uroteuthis was corroborated. The alias column is not an exhaustive taxonomic revision. Caranx kalla remains without an uncertain synonym assertion.

Separately named catch does not exclude a taxon from an unidentified aggregate. Constant weights use identified catch only within the same family/order. Generic demersals include Benthic Omnivores at low confidence.

nodes.label: Karnataka2000 carangid size and diet analogues

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 geographic prefixes
nodes.rationale: 29 of 50 groups carry geographic numeric prefixes. Region 1 covers Maldives/open waters; region 2 Bangladesh, east India and Sri Lanka; region 3 Myanmar, Thailand, west Malaysia, west Indonesia and Andaman/Nicobar. Coastal pools are relatively isolated; unprefixed stocks span the study area. 2-3 Hilsa and 2-3 Indian mackerel already encode cross-region stocks.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 Region 1 catch exclusion
nodes.rationale: The 6,205,051 km2 study area includes Maldives/high seas outside LME_034. Maldives at 72.5-73.8 E lies west of the LME bounding box beginning 77.57 E; the region 1 high seas have zero shelf. Region 1 shelf/benthic/zooplankton pools are excluded from catch candidates; regions 2 and 3 represent this catch area.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 region 2 and 3 biomass weighting
nodes.rationale: Prefixed taxa split across 2 X | 3 X using model_biomass. groups_df biomass is already per whole-study-area, so ratios represent total standing stock. The 1978 model_catch alternative was rejected as a snapshot of moving fisheries and a non-independent SAU reconstruction. The author spreads coastal diets by shelf area, 23.6/76.4% across regions 2 and 3. Cross-model interpretation: Both fix apportionment from one period over 70 catch years but weight different axes: geographic regions versus ontogenetic stages.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 regional weight sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Biomass versus catch weighting raises taxon SPPR about 10-40%. The original all-region-2 mapping omitted region 3 and understated many demersal/benthic PPR estimates about twofold. Region 3 SPPR is typically 2-5 times region 2. Weight basis is the principal reviewable judgment.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 Appendix membership authority
nodes.rationale: Guenette 2013 is the sole membership authority: Appendix A1.1 catch allocation, A1.2 area, A1.3 species, and Table 16 biomass. Dutta 2023 and Karim 2018/2019 describe different local models and do not define these groups. 259 of 315 taxa have direct author catch allocations.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 unavailable companion materials
nodes.rationale: The Guenette 2014 user guide and later report edition were sought but not obtained because the BOBLME host failed. Membership remains available in the 2013 appendices. The potential model database and regional diet/landings breakdown remain unavailable.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 mapping coverage and regional uncertainty
nodes.rationale: 100% mapped, no unresolved or inherited rows, and 30 of 50 groups carry catch. 239 taxa and 83.1% catch are composites, mainly regions 2/3. 259 taxa and 74.2% tonnage are source-confirmed with zero contradictions. The member list expands author labels across all three regions and validates guild identity, not the chosen geographic shares.
nodes.norm_label: bayofbengal1978 mapping coverage and regional uncertainty

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 coarse catch candidate constraints
nodes.rationale: Unidentified marine fish, 46.5 million tonnes and 18.5% of catch, uses four demersal/benthic finfish pools across regions 2/3 after narrowing the author residual by SAU habitat. Scombridae includes Tuna-like, Coastal scombrids and 2-3 Indian mackerel. Flatfishes span SM inv/SM pisc. Compound source allocations retain all compartments.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 species-specific source precedence
nodes.rationale: Polynemus paradiseus goes to SM pisc because Appendix A1.3 explicitly names the species there, overriding the A1.1 genus allocation to L pisc/SM inv. Balistidae analogues follow Abalistes stellaris in SM pisc. Compound family allocations cannot be collapsed to the first group. Cross-model interpretation: Source-specific species membership takes precedence over broad family, genus or common-name assignments.

nodes.label: BayOfBengal1978 fixed regional weights limitation
nodes.rationale: Uncertainty lies in region 2/3 shares even with no unresolved catch. Static 1978 regional structure across 1950-2019 cannot capture the eastward fishery shift. A time-varying split requires EEZ-resolved catch absent from the repository. Extracted taxon_descr remains empty in this source snapshot.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 payload and 1963 metadata conflict
nodes.rationale: All eleven Christensen Table II biomasses match the printed 1980 column; ten fail 1963, and Benthos 33 matches both. The Ecobase description says 1980 but filename/model_year say 1963. This identity conflict is preserved, with parameters and filename untouched, and the warning must accompany downstream results.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 incomplete numerical source provenance
nodes.rationale: The original article full HTML was read through the author page; original PDF requests returned 403. Group prose pp.130-132 and Tables I/II were inspected. No complete B/PB/QB/EE/diet table is printed, so full numerical re-extraction remains unavailable. No original PDF retrieval is claimed.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 shelf geographic transfer
nodes.rationale: The source domain is the 10-50 m Gulf of Thailand shelf. Applying all LME_035 catch is a geographic/habitat transfer. Pauly and Chuenpagdee 2003 provide supporting lineage evidence. Vibunpant 2003 is a distinct 40-group 1973 model and was excluded as direct evidence.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 illustrative source membership precedence
nodes.rationale: Christensen p.130 supplies 38 member rows including repeated juvenile memberships and sardine/anchovy common names. Important components are illustrative, not exhaustive. Exact/genus/family source decisions outrank SAU. Normalising Ephinephelus to Epinephelus and Plectorhynchus to Plectorhinchus is explicit; Tachysuridea remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 source-constrained family unions
nodes.rationale: Sciaenidae/Pennahia, Lethrinus and Psettodes are medium demersal piscivores; Priacanthus small demersal piscivores; Scolopsis/Upeneus medium benthivores. Nemipteridae spans Scolopsis and Nemipterus groups. Clupeiformes retains large-piscivore Chirocentrus stages and small pelagics. 66 source-constrained cases were reviewed; intersection-only membership validation is insufficient.

nodes.label: Thailand1980 juvenile grouper and snapper stages
nodes.rationale: The source explicitly splits juvenile grouper AND snapper despite the shortened Juv. groupers JSON label. Shark, large-piscivore and grouper/snapper unaged catches use fixed model_catch weights with zero recorded juvenile catch. These are not historical catch-age observations.
nodes.norm_label: thailand1980 juvenile grouper and snapper stages

nodes.label: Ecopath database JSON round trip
nodes.rationale: database_json.py rebuilds the downstream database JSON from the eight files, not model.json, then writes a reconstructed workbook, MASS_BALANCE.md and ewe_conversion.log. nodes.label: Unknown values distinct from software defaults
nodes.rationale: Blank import cells mean the source states nothing, database -9999 means unknown, printed 0 means zero. Software defaults and a balance checker suggested BA are not source evidence. Preserve precision and provenance; leave ambiguity blank and flag it.
nodes.norm_label: unknown values distinct from software defaults

nodes.label: Unknown biomass accumulation treatment
nodes.rationale: Search mortality tables, prose, time series and figures before diagnosing balance discrepancies. Blank/missing BA leaves biomass_accum and biomass_accum_rate both -9999. If source states one form, preserve it and derive the other only internally/database output with logged biomass/habitat scaling. Never fill import BA using an equation's suggested closing value.

nodes.label: Ecopath structural and arithmetic validation
nodes.rationale: validate.py checks numbering, diet sums within ±0.01, detritus fate sums, fleet totals, quotes and CRLF. massbalance_check.py recomputes EE=(Y+BA+predation)/(B(P/B)), respiration, gross efficiency, detritus closure and consumer diet completeness. Investigate flagged cells against rendered sources; retain genuine rounding drift.

nodes.label: Ecopath database balance verdicts
nodes.rationale: BALANCED means no failures or undecidables; INDETERMINATE means no failures but an EE mismatch with unknown BA; NOT BALANCED includes known-BA production overconsumption, nonpositive respiration or impossible detritus closure. A match without BA is consistent with steady state, not proof. Verdicts remain in log/MASS_BALANCE.md, not model JSON.

nodes.label: Habitat-area to model-area balance conversion
nodes.rationale: Absolute BA from files is per habitat area and multiplied by habitat area to align with JSON biomass, preserving biomass_accum/biomass=biomass_accum_rate. Database check uses model-area biomass/catch/BA; file massbalance_check uses habitat-area basis. They agree for habitat fraction one, but database check matches imported EwE area scaling otherwise.

nodes.label: EwE documented import defaults
nodes.rationale: GS 0.2 for energy-currency models; 0.4 suggested for zooplankton grazing phytoplankton; BA zero, habitat area one, catch/migration/prices/import zero; detritus-fate remainder exported. Defaults describe importer behavior, not source-stated data. All four B/PB/QB/EE can imply estimated net migration omitted by massbalance_check.

nodes.label: EwE User Guide Ecopath Input
nodes.rationale: Referenced for software defaults and sanity ranges: https://pressbooks.bccampus.ca/eweguide/chapter/ecopath-input/ ; EwE textbook https://pressbooks.bccampus.ca/ewemodel/ .

nodes.label: Ecopath physiological sanity ranges
nodes.rationale: P/Q 0.1-0.3 typical consumers, fish R/B 1-10/year, copepod R/B about 50-100/year. Positive respiration needs P/Q<1-GS. Ranges trigger source rendering and header re-checks, never replacement values or midpoints.

nodes.label: Ecopath extraction provenance reporting
nodes.rationale: REPORT.md records source locations, non-table derivations, source searches behind blanks, values matching software defaults and ambiguity. MASTER_INDEX.md tracks each model's status. Report distinguishes paper statements, inherited information and explicit conventions.

nodes.label: Ecopath model formulation reference
nodes.rationale: Ecopath is a static food-web mass-balance snapshot for a defined area/period, solved as linear equations. Ecosim adds dynamics; Ecospace adds space. Biomass uses wet-weight t/km² and rates/year.

nodes.label: Ecopath production balance
nodes.rationale: B_i(P/B)_i = Y_i + sum_j B_j(Q/B)_j DC_ji + E_i + BA_i + B_i(P/B)_i(1-EE_i). E is emigration minus immigration; catch Y includes landings and discards. The older simplified EE check printed in this reference omits both E and BA, unlike the current extraction workflow's BA-aware equation.

nodes.label: Ecopath consumption energy balance
nodes.rationale: Q=P+R+U, U=GS*Q; R/B=(Q/B)(1-GS)-(P/B). Positive respiration requires P/Q<1-GS; net efficiency <=1. Primary producers lack consumption/GS and detritus lacks production/respiration.

nodes.label: Ecopath three-of-four parameter rule
nodes.rationale: Ecopath requires three of B, P/B, Q/B, EE and a diet for every consumer, solving the fourth. Systematic blanks can be model-estimated parameters; fewer than three prompts prose investigation. All four may mix model inputs and outputs.

nodes.label: Ecopath derived versus reported quantities
nodes.rationale: Reported TL, GE, mortalities, respiration, omnivory and detrital flows may be outputs; extract them if present, never recompute to fill source gaps. Ecosim vulnerabilities and network indices are outside eight-file input scope; keep every multi-stanza life stage as its own group.

nodes.label: Ecopath detritus and fishery accounting
nodes.rationale: Other mortality, unassimilated food and discards feed detritus pools via Detritus_fate; outflow is consumption/export. Landings leave system, discards commonly enter offal. Total catch without discard split goes in Landings with note. Absolute tonnes must be converted using model area.

nodes.label: Unverified Ecopath formulation citations
nodes.rationale: Reference names Polovina ECOPATH, Christensen & Pauly 1992 Ecopath II and Christensen & Walters 2004 EwE synthesis; explicitly says citations were recalled from memory, not database-verified, and migration/BA sign conventions require checking.

nodes.label: EwE import-file format contract
nodes.rationale: One stable directory per model identifier/name/year. UTF-8 without BOM, CRLF including final line, no quotes, exact template headers, contiguous consistent group numbers, source-printed number precision. Null/omitted JSON keys become blanks; zero remains zero.

nodes.label: EwE prey-by-consumer diet matrix
nodes.rationale: Diet_composition has prey rows and consumer-number columns, trailing Import, Sum and (1-Sum) rows. JSON diet is predator-keyed with prey-string keys plus import. Explicit row lists preserve intentional differences between full group list and prey/catch rows.

nodes.label: Ecopath model report and extraction-set index
nodes.rationale: REPORT.md requires source tables/layout, BA searches, prose derivations, conventions, deliberate blanks, conflicts and validation/mass-balance findings. MASTER_INDEX statuses complete, partial, excluded, pending must be updated with the model.
nodes.norm_label: ecopath model report and extraction-set index

nodes.label: Ecopath parameter conventions reference
nodes.rationale: Preserve the source parameter rather than deriving Z/PB, GE or TL to fill blanks. Blank, printed zero and analyst convention remain distinct. Software defaults explain consequences but do not supply source data.

nodes.label: Restricted zooplankton unassimilated-consumption convention
nodes.rationale: Use table GS first, then prose/stated assimilation complement, then explicit project convention. 0.4 only for unambiguously small zooplankton; 0.35 only unambiguous zooplankton-like groups. Ambiguous Zooplankton, Plankton, Invertebrates and Other pelagics stay blank. Project rules are narrower than EwE suggestions.

nodes.label: Biomass accumulation sign-convention review
nodes.rationale: Reference says negative BA is declining biomass but also says it raises printed EE relative to steady-state recomputation; its own later B(P/B)EE=Y+BA+predation equation makes that sign explanation inconsistent if other terms are held fixed. Preserve the stated negative-decline meaning and flag the explanatory sign discrepancy for review.

nodes.label: Ecopath parameter provenance categories
nodes.rationale: REPORT.md distinguishes tabulated, prose-derived, model-estimated and convention-derived values; any arithmetic and source locations remain explicit.

nodes.label: Ecopath source-bundle inventory
nodes.rationale: Record each file's role, model coverage, content locations and authority before row extraction. Distinct parameterizations get distinct model directories even with identical groups. Inventory hidden spreadsheet sheets; notebook/script output is derived, not automatically paper-stated.

nodes.label: Ecopath source conflict authority guide
nodes.rationale: Investigate author machine-readable tables, final tables, numeric prose/footnotes, figures and prior calculations in that order. This is guidance, not permission to discard conflicting evidence. Record both values/locations and chosen rationale; never average, normalize or silently substitute. Search every assigned file before declaring absence.

nodes.label: Coordinate-aware Ecopath PDF extraction
nodes.rationale: pdfgrid reconstructs columns from word bounding boxes using PyMuPDF with Poppler fallback. Render first, inspect raw coordinates, anchor on header numbers and then export. pdftotext -layout may silently move real numbers under wrong predators.

nodes.label: Anchored PDF diet-column reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Prefer numeric header anchors to prevent sparse columns disappearing. Match left/centre/right edges. merge_gap is about 2.0 pt for normal tables and about 0.4 for dense matrices (Azores/Mauritania); fused numeric cells require lower gap, split labels can be rejoined.

nodes.label: Rendered-page validation for numeric extraction
nodes.rationale: Preserve sources, rotate working copies and verify orientation. Inspect flagged numbers against page images at >=200 dpi; scanned/manual transcription uses 300 dpi and is reported. Re-extraction is not independent visual verification.

nodes.label: Ecopath prose and footnote extraction
nodes.rationale: Tables may omit parameters stated in prose. Resolve see text/voir texte pointers before reading cells; prose_sweep proposes passages rather than extracted values. Sweep whole chapter, then repeat with remaining blanks and group names.

nodes.label: Quantitative limits of prose-derived values
nodes.rationale: Scope every statement to specific groups. Entirely/exclusively yields diet 1.0; mainly/predominantly supplies no numeric proportion. Keep partial stated diets without filling residual. Distinguish discard share of catch versus of landings; record assimilation complements and unit arithmetic.

nodes.label: Table-footnote conflict precedence
nodes.rationale: Prefer table for tabulated data unless a footnote explicitly redirects to prose. Prefer methods for assumptions and explicit later/specific revisions when present. Record alternatives and choice; never choose what balances best.

nodes.label: Figure-derived parameter precision
nodes.rationale: Digitize only against labeled grids at 300 dpi, preserve one or two supported significant figures, do not extrapolate or read log axes by eye. Falling biomass implies negative BA. If one significant figure is unreliable, leave blank and report; derived slopes retain endpoints/year/arithmetic.

nodes.label: Ecopath table layout mapping
nodes.rationale: Read complete caption/footnotes, write header-to-field mapping before values, verify one row arithmetically, identify rows by name and count expected groups/consumers. This guards against pattern completion from prior tables.

nodes.label: Ecopath table structure and notation conventions
nodes.rationale: Join continued or column-block tables by prey label, anchor numeric header lines, preserve adult/juvenile subcolumns, transpose in code and merge wrapped names. Parenthesized estimates retain provenance; dashes/NA/trace bounds are not silently zero; blank diets preserve source convention.
nodes.norm_label: ecopath table structure and notation conventions

nodes.label: Ecopath source-unit conversion contract
nodes.rationale: Use source model area for absolute tonnes; kg/ha divides by 10 to t/km²; daily rates multiply by 365. Wet/dry/carbon conversion needs the paper's factor. Seasonal aggregation requires stated method. Log every factor; ambiguous units or layout remain flagged rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Paper-to-PPR taxonomy handoff
nodes.rationale: Capture membership while the source is open so Taxonomy.xlsx (seq, group_name, taxon_descr) flows into database taxon_descr then groups_df. Explicit membership evidence can replace later guesswork; not documented means completed source search. JSON-only Ecobase route uses tools/apply_taxonomy.py.

nodes.label: Named-model SPPR wrapper
nodes.rationale: tools/run_sppr.py reads only named JSONs and writes groups_df, sppr_all, sppr_inner, sppr_PP, model_health and run_notes. Heavy methods have time budgets; timeouts/errors stay NaN. --in-place replaces an authorized committed workbook; otherwise stage/compare. Refresh mapping work order after replacement.

nodes.label: SPPR legacy script side-effect boundary
nodes.rationale: Never shell-execute PPREstimation/create_PPRS_excel.py, even --help: main ignores arguments and overwrites pilot workbooks. Use wrapper API path and keep Jensen behavior unchanged.

nodes.label: Per-method model-health review
nodes.rationale: Clean extraction/import is insufficient for fitness; examine balance, diet sums and divergent TE_option. Record verdict in data/model_selection.xlsx. NaN method results are unknown/failed, never zero.

nodes.label: Authoritative groups_df mapping join
nodes.rationale: Model group names come verbatim from PPREstimation/output/top10/<model>.xlsx groups_df. Catch source is SeaAroundUsExtraction/data/catch_by_taxon_year/<unit>.csv.gz. Use actual taxon_descr plus cited sources, distinguishing empty extraction gaps from not-documented source-search results.

nodes.label: Mapping work-order preparation
nodes.rationale: prepare_mapping.py writes WORK_ORDER.md with usability, exact group names, TL, biomass, catches and catch-taxon ranks/coarse flags; stubs preserve one row per catch taxon. Check model selection before mapping.

nodes.label: Source membership precedence in catch mapping
nodes.rationale: Read model paper/supplements/diets and adopted predecessors. Transcribe a source species-to-group table before mapping. Evidence order: explicit member, accepted/synonym match, containment, habitat-size-guild with TL corroboration, inherited classification, analogue, apportionment, unresolved. TL alone never selects a guild.
nodes.norm_label: source membership precedence in catch mapping

nodes.label: Membership source-review accountability
nodes.rationale: Make actual download attempts for identifiable missing supplements; retain filename/URL/result. Distinguish direct/adopted source, supporting regional source and analyst inference. Never claim a supplement was read from its citation alone.

nodes.label: Catch-tonnage mapping coverage target
nodes.rationale: Target 95% tonnage on named groups, prioritize high-catch taxa and use validator's largest unresolved records as work list. Complete only after PASS or justified remaining source-incompatible catch; FAIL cannot be reported complete.

nodes.label: Model PPR workbook construction and verification
nodes.rationale: tools/build_model_workbook.py refuses unknown group names and writes data/<unit>/models/<model>.xlsx plus resolved.csv with actual weights. tools/verify_model_workbook.py re-derives formulas and reconciles per-taxon/aggregate sheets. Mapping CSV preserves original order; workbooks are generated.
nodes.norm_label: model ppr workbook construction and verification

nodes.label: Coarse-taxon apportionment playbook
nodes.rationale: Coarse catch labels genuinely spanning groups should be apportioned instead of discarded; Unresolved is appropriate when the model has no compatible home. Historical baseline unresolved tonnage: Arabian Sea 21.8%, Bay of Bengal 22.3%, East China Sea 22.1%, under older table counts.

nodes.label: Evidence-constrained composite candidate sets
nodes.rationale: Apply documented source member placement and accepted synonyms before inferential taxonomy/habitat/size/commercial filters. Check every composite member even after validator acceptance. SAU class suggests center/adjacent size bands, not unrelated habitats; Other fishes & inverts excludes nothing. A split represents a genuinely broad taxon, not uncertainty about one correct home.

nodes.label: Constant composite weighting and fallback
nodes.rationale: Blank weights use identified-catch composition summed over the period. Weights stay constant across years so PPR=catch(taxon,year)*SPPR(taxon,method). For empty/circular composition use model_catch or model_biomass; fallback chain is model_catch -> model_biomass -> equal. Record actual basis. Explicit stated proportions and equal shares are also supported.

nodes.label: Composite mapping confidence contract
nodes.rationale: Medium for well-founded set with data-derived weights; low for wide sets/equal weights; high only for stated species composition. Never assign high when script computed the weights.

nodes.label: Taxonomic family unions and dedicated stocks
nodes.rationale: For family/order labels include all model groups with source-compatible members, including dedicated single-species groups inside that family plus appropriate general guilds. Batoidea cannot silently become Sharks. Mollusca may span benthic molluscs and cephalopods; Decapoda spans compatible crustacean groups.
nodes.norm_label: taxonomic family unions and dedicated stocks

nodes.label: Ecopath grouping-axis archetypes
nodes.rationale: Determine taxonomy, size/habitat, feeding guild, spatial/depth stratum and life stage before mapping. Record prefixes, stocks vs pools, catch-capable groups and source area relative to catch unit.

nodes.label: Feeding-guild model membership evidence
nodes.rationale: East China Sea guild groups need species lists, often in DOCX supplement; diet matrix constrains membership. Families spanning guilds require source-constrained composites; same TL can describe distinct diets.

nodes.label: Spatial-stratum composite weighting
nodes.rationale: Bay of Bengal prefixes represent subareas/depth; assigning all whole-LME catch to stratum 2 is a historical error. Taxa spanning strata use model_biomass when catch does not distinguish strata; restricted taxa use justified single strata, range names and unprefixed groups preserve source meaning.

nodes.label: Life-stage stock composite weighting
nodes.rationale: Species catch not separated by age/stage maps across stock stages. model_catch best captures selectivity when stage landings are given; otherwise model_biomass.

nodes.label: Catch-capable functional groups
nodes.rationale: Detritus and import cannot take catch; PP excluded except genuine harvested seaweed. Zooplankton, meiobenthos and microbial groups require evidence of actual landed fisheries.

nodes.label: Species-to-group mapping output contract
nodes.rationale: Plain CSV has taxon, common_name, functional_group, commercial_group, group, weights, confidence, evidence, explanation; original taxon rows/order preserved. Group strings must match groups_df exactly; composites use pipe-separated names and composite_split; Unresolved pairs with none/unresolved.

nodes.label: Published member-table validation contract
nodes.rationale: members.csv stores printed_name, accepted_name, group_name and source_page. Both printed/accepted names are indexed. Contradiction is an error. Arabian Sea CMFRI Bulletin 51 had 129 species under 24 groups; checking caught five wrong placements totaling 2.3% catch caused by preferring SAU class to the model.

nodes.label: Group dictionary source-relationship fields
nodes.rationale: groups.csv retains every group, grouping_basis, explicit_members, supporting_taxa, membership_source, source_relationship, source_location, source_url and notes. Relationship is direct source, supporting regional source or analyst inference. Notes report geography, model axis, obtained/missing supplements and limitations.

nodes.label: Source geography before filename interpretation
nodes.rationale: Scope example is the 111,932 km² model off the country Guinea versus whole Guinea Current LME. Okhotsk NE names the detailed whole-Sea Ecopath model, not a northeastern subregion. Verify source geography before interpreting filename prefixes.

nodes.label: Codex Ecopath extraction workflow
nodes.rationale: Preserves source numbers, missingness and provenance through eight EwE import files, database JSON, round-trip workbook and mass-balance reports. Standalone extraction leaves group taxonomy to the combined skill.

nodes.label: Codex Ecopath paper to PPR skill
nodes.rationale: Routes the requested stage only: paper extraction, group taxonomy, named-model SPPR or catch-to-group PPR. Preserves exact source membership, missing results and both Jensen calculations.
nodes.norm_label: codex ecopath paper to ppr skill

nodes.label: Codex Ecopath paper to PPR interface
nodes.rationale: Display name Ecopath Paper to PPR; default prompt continues the requested extraction, taxonomy, SPPR or PPR stage; implicit invocation enabled.
nodes.norm_label: codex ecopath paper to ppr interface

nodes.label: Codex combined paper to PPR workflow
nodes.rationale: Four-stage pipeline reuses close reading of the source paper, capturing membership once rather than reconstructing it later without the extractor's notes.
nodes.norm_label: codex combined paper to ppr workflow

nodes.label: Codex EwE species to group mapper skill
nodes.rationale: Builds an auditable mapping per model, prioritizing printed members over habitat or trophic-level inference; requires the repository's exact groups and validates final PPR.
nodes.norm_label: codex ewe species to group mapper skill

nodes.label: Codex EwE species mapper interface
nodes.rationale: EwE Species-to-Group Mapper UI, bundled icon and auditable-evidence default prompt; implicit invocation enabled for ChatGPT, Codex, API and Atlas.

nodes.label: Codex EwE catch mapping workflow
nodes.rationale: Joins Sea Around Us catch taxa to exact Ecopath functional groups so group SPPR becomes PPR per taxon and year; targets mapped tonnage rather than taxon count.

nodes.label: Combined paper to PPR source router
nodes.rationale: Shared combined-skill router assembles extraction, taxonomy, SPPR and mapping into one source-aware workflow. It also supports requests for only one stage.
nodes.norm_label: combined paper to ppr source router

nodes.label: Combined group taxonomy stage
nodes.rationale: Captures source-defined group membership while the paper is open; provides both the extraction-folder Taxonomy.xlsx route and the database-JSON-only route.

nodes.label: PPR atlas network metric controls
nodes.rationale: HTML controls select PPR, method ratios, recycling b or living rho; All/Inner/PP scope; GE/TE diagnostics. Gray means unselected or unavailable within the explicit pilot rule.

nodes.label: PPRCalculator SPPR mathematical methods reference
nodes.rationale: Explains trophic-chain and flow-network SPPR, transfer efficiency, recycling, Monte Carlo uncertainty, diagnostics and catch footprints.

nodes.label: ModelData and PPRCalculator user guide
nodes.rationale: Practical constructors, inputs, model completion, method parameters and diagnostics. Some older explanatory claims conflict with the more detailed methods reference and are retained as reviewable ambiguity.

nodes.label: Root project integration overview
nodes.rationale: Current project entry point links INTEGRATION_COMPLETION.md as the source for present results; CODEX_TAKEOVER and HANDOFF are historical records.

nodes.label: Data integration spine overview
nodes.rationale: Joins catch, region identity, model selection, SPPR, mapping and NPP through unit_id while referencing bulk inputs rather than duplicating them.

nodes.label: Codex integration takeover review
nodes.rationale: Initial inspected state is retained as history. Its final addendum marks tasks 1-5 complete and points to INTEGRATION_COMPLETION.md for current outcomes.

nodes.label: Isolated Saygu new paper validation report
nodes.rationale: Documents a complete computational paper-to-PPR test for East Coast of Scotland 1991-1995. It is not an adopted production North Sea estimate.

nodes.label: Historical integration structural verification record
nodes.rationale: Earlier final verification records 185 Sea Around Us tests, 8 atlas tests and the unchanged PPREstimation baseline of 1 failure, 76 passes and 18 errors; this is distinct from the later pilot completion suite.

nodes.label: Claude and Codex skill layout implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Completed plan for shared domain resources, agent-specific entry points and six packages; preserves research, Jensen behavior and existing work.
nodes.norm_label: claude and codex skill layout implementation plan

nodes.rationale: Authorized tasks 1-5 and scope/ratio/recycling additions precede broader coverage expansion; requires independent verification and keeps new-paper validation isolated.

nodes.label: Independent Guinea combined arm mapping notes
nodes.rationale: Isolated mapping uses shared audited membership and public source checks but did not consult production decisions; documents geographic transfer, composite assumptions and unsupported taxa.
nodes.norm_label: independent guinea combined arm mapping notes

nodes.label: Independent Guinea combined arm results report
nodes.rationale: All 375 taxa processed; PASS with zero member contradictions and 99.665235% mapped tonnage. This is joinability evidence, not ecological accuracy.

nodes.rationale: Current authority: tasks 1-5 and scope, ratio, recycling views are complete; task 6 coverage expansion has not started. Supersedes older open-work status without erasing history.

nodes.label: Source faithful extraction and unknown values
nodes.rationale: Numbers stay as printed; missing cells are not filled from defaults, similar groups or balance-derived suggestions. Preserve paper-stated, adopted-default and inferred provenance distinctly.
nodes.norm_label: source faithful extraction and unknown values

nodes.label: Coordinate based Ecopath table extraction
nodes.rationale: Word bounding boxes and explicit header mapping prevent silently shifted PDF columns. Read captions and footnotes, match group names and test identities before extraction.

nodes.label: Eight file EwE round trip validation
nodes.rationale: Extraction JSON writes eight import files; database JSON is rebuilt from those files, so writer errors and manual CSV edits are independently visible. Emits reconstructed workbook, MASS_BALANCE and conversion log.
nodes.norm_label: eight file ewe round trip validation

nodes.label: Unknown biomass accumulation preservation
nodes.rationale: Search mortality tables, prose, figures and time series first. Blank BA remains unknown and database -9999; EwE's zero default is not source evidence. Suggested closing BA is a prompt to inspect the source, never an input.

nodes.label: Ecopath mass balance verdicts
nodes.rationale: BALANCED means no failure or undecidable check; INDETERMINATE preserves unknown-BA ambiguity; NOT BALANCED records a known inconsistency. Verdicts remain in reports rather than the loaded model JSON.

nodes.label: Taxonomy membership provenance chain
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy.xlsx -> database taxon_descr -> groups_df -> explicit_member evidence captures membership once and prevents later mappings from reverting to guesswork.

nodes.label: Three column Taxonomy workbook contract
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy.xlsx contains seq, exact group_name and taxon_descr in that order. The converter indexes column two and reads the last column, so an extra column would change the meaning.

nodes.label: JSON only Ecobase taxonomy application
nodes.rationale: Finished Ecobase JSONs need no invented extraction folder. Prepare an exact seq/group_name/taxon_descr sidecar, apply with tools/apply_taxonomy.py, inspect staged SPPR, then refresh the mapping work order after repository replacement.

nodes.label: Source defined model profile
nodes.rationale: Record grouping axis, prefixes, model area, catch-taking groups, single stocks, pools and membership evidence. Never infer geographic fractions from filenames.

nodes.label: Documented absence of group membership
nodes.rationale: Use 'not documented' after an actual paper/supplement search to distinguish searched absence from unexamined missing data.

nodes.label: Exact functional group join contract
nodes.rationale: groups_df is authoritative and joins on group_name character for character; model taxa, geography and group structure cannot be transferred from an example workbook.

nodes.label: Catch tonnage mapping coverage target
nodes.rationale: Target 95% mapped catch tonnage. Taxon counts can be misleading because rare unmapped taxa contribute little PPR; unsupported taxa remain unresolved rather than forcing the target.

nodes.label: Source member evidence before inference
nodes.rationale: Transcribe member tables before mapping; explicit or synonym membership outranks containment, habitat and feeding analogues. Never choose a feeding guild from TL alone.

nodes.label: Safe named model SPPR regeneration
nodes.rationale: Use tools/run_sppr.py with explicit model stems, staged output and comparison. Heavy-method failure or timeout stays NaN. Direct shell invocation of create_PPRS_excel.py, even --help, runs an unintended broad overwrite.

nodes.label: Configuration health before catch mapping
nodes.rationale: A clean extraction and import do not imply a numerically usable model. Inspect model_health and usable selection before deriving mapped PPR.

nodes.label: Shared Claude and Codex skill distributions
nodes.rationale: Claude standalone directories own domain resources; combined-src owns combined routing/taxonomy; codex-src owns concise entry points and interface metadata. Corresponding resources and all six archives are checked deterministically.
nodes.norm_label: shared claude and codex skill distributions

nodes.label: Taxonomy sidecar exclusion from mapping discovery
nodes.rationale: A taxonomy CSV is group membership metadata, not a catch-taxonomy mapping; exclude .taxonomy.csv alongside other sidecars from mapping discovery and ecosystem counts.
nodes.norm_label: taxonomy sidecar exclusion from mapping discovery

nodes.label: Specific primary production required
nodes.rationale: Units of basal production per unit of group production; catch-weighted sums give PPR. Trophic-level methods return scalar costs; network methods resolve basal sources and actual food-web topology.

nodes.label: Production normalized diet matrix
nodes.rationale: A_ik = DC_ik / TE_i; under ecotrophic TE this equals Z_ik/(P_i-M0_i). Terminal-source identity rows yield a nullspace basis with one column per basal source.

nodes.label: Transfer efficiency accounting conventions
nodes.rationale: GE=p/q; TE=GE*EE; With Egestion=p/(q-egestion); global uses a fixed or model-weighted scalar. The choice changes both path weights and detritus accounting.

nodes.label: Pauly and Christensen 1995 trophic chain method
nodes.rationale: SPPR_i=(1/TE)^(TL_i-1), using each group's continuous TL with global TE. Does not offer a source decomposition.
nodes.norm_label: pauly and christensen 1995 trophic chain method

nodes.label: Integer trophic level interpolation
nodes.rationale: Blend the bracketing integer-TL chain costs. Because exponentiation is convex, the direct fractional exponent is below the interpolation between adjacent integer levels.

nodes.label: EwE simple path SPPR method
nodes.rationale: Enumerates every simple food-chain path with full diet weights. Repeated-node paths are excluded, so cycling and cannibalism are undercounted; use_EE scales the focal-group row.

nodes.label: Ulanowicz cycle pruned SPPR method
nodes.rationale: Deletes weakest-link cycle edges without renormalizing remaining diet weights, then solves a nullspace. Equals simple-path EwE only for acyclic webs and is not the full cycle-summed answer.

nodes.label: Leontief 2015 SPPR method
nodes.rationale: Dissolves detritus columns back to PP-origin flows and uses (I-A)^-1 to sum all path lengths, including cycles, when the relevant spectral radius is below one.

nodes.label: SPPR_new numeric food web solver
nodes.rationale: Solves the full living-network nullspace with detritus as a temporary basal source, then resolves detritus values with explicit retention, openness and pooling controls.

nodes.label: SPPR_symbolic source accounting solver
nodes.rationale: Symbolic counterpart to SPPR_new shares detritus controls, with imported diet as a separately inferred DC-weighted source or as a PP-like basal source.

nodes.label: Single detritus SPPR fixed point
nodes.rationale: sppr_det=a+b*sppr_det, giving a/(1-b). a carries non-detritus-origin input and b the consumer-mediated return of detritus-origin material. A finite algebraic result at b>=1 need not be physical.

nodes.label: Coupled detritus recycling system
nodes.rationale: For multiple pools, x=c+B*x and (I-B)x=c. Each B entry composes living-network detritus dependence with mortality/egestion routed back into a pool.

nodes.label: Detritus recycling gain b
nodes.rationale: b=rho(diag(theta)*B), measured before solve-versus-pool fallback. b<1 is the detritus convergence condition. Under TE there is no recycling matrix and reported b=0 with a note.

nodes.label: Living network spectral radius rho living
nodes.rationale: rho_living=rho(A_LL), where A_LL contains living-to-living predation and cannibalism. rho_living>=1 corrupts the living basis used to construct B and invalidates interpretation of b.
nodes.norm_label: living network spectral radius rho living

nodes.label: Convergence necessary but insufficient for SPPR validity
nodes.rationale: Both b and rho_living must be below one. Near-one amplification, excessive detritus SPPR, source negatives, input imbalance and PP budget gaps can still make a convergent result unusable.
nodes.norm_label: convergence necessary but insufficient for sppr validity

nodes.label: Detritus retention and openness transforms
nodes.rationale: recycling_loss dampens B by diag(theta); source_dilution also replaces c by theta*c+external_sppr*(1-theta). External SPPR changes c rather than the convergence gain.

nodes.label: TE detritus direct source credit
nodes.rationale: Ecotrophic TE already treats consumer mortality as lost, so only direct PP/import material credits detritus. There is no consumer-return recycling fixed point in this convention.

nodes.label: Single detritus EE zero recredit

nodes.rationale: Records taxa included within each functional group; the historical handoff identified systematic missing taxon_descr/taxons_included content, motivating explicit taxonomy extraction.

nodes.label: Authoritative groups_df group names
nodes.rationale: Downstream joins must match group_name character for character; near-misses would drop PPR and are rejected.

nodes.label: Per-model scoped SPPR and health workbooks
nodes.rationale: Contains groups_df, sppr_all, sppr_inner, sppr_PP, model_health and run_notes. NaN means unavailable, never zero.
nodes.norm_label: per-model scoped sppr and health workbooks

nodes.label: Separate per-model PPR workbooks
nodes.source_location: §4 Integration layer; §8 Traps; §16 Site-wide carbon display
nodes.rationale: Distinct models of one ecosystem get separate workbooks; results must not be averaged. Source XLSX PPR remains wet weight under the latest display policy; site source-workbook links disclose that distinction.

nodes.label: Taxon-to-group mapping CSV contract
nodes.rationale: Rows contain taxon, common_name, functional_group, commercial_group, group, weights, confidence, evidence, explanation; group can be one name, pipe-separated candidates or Unresolved.

nodes.label: Mapping evidence and generated artifact family
nodes.rationale: WORK_ORDER, mapping CSV, members.csv, taxonomy.csv, groups.csv, notes.md and resolved.csv separate decisions, source evidence and computed weights.
nodes.norm_label: mapping evidence and generated artifact family

nodes.label: Composite catch-taxon apportionment
nodes.rationale: Broad catch labels spanning legitimate groups are split rather than dropped. Candidate groups are chosen by the mapper, and weight basis is recorded.

nodes.label: Recorded apportionment weight fallback chain
nodes.rationale: Observed identified catch composition → model catch → model biomass → equal shares.

nodes.label: Fixed catch composition apportionment
nodes.rationale: Keeping weights fixed gives each taxon one SPPR per method so annual PPR stays catch(taxon,year) × SPPR(taxon,method).

nodes.label: Unresolved mapping as a scientific exclusion
nodes.rationale: Unresolved means outside supported model coverage, not merely difficult to decide. Honest exclusions with reasons are preferred to plausible guesses.
nodes.norm_label: unresolved mapping as a scientific exclusion

nodes.label: Coverage measured in catch tonnage
nodes.rationale: Taxon counts can misrepresent PPR support: the historical example has 44% unresolved taxa but 90% resolved tonnage. A 95% target is not a quota.

nodes.label: Publication species-to-group member tables
nodes.rationale: Paper-specific membership takes precedence over generic size/habitat inference; validator checks printed and accepted names and genus-level unions.

nodes.label: CMFRI Bulletin 51 ecological groupings
nodes.rationale: 129 species under 24 groups; historical source recheck identified five wrong assignments carrying 2.3% of catch. Formio niger and Parastromateus niger are the same taxon.

nodes.label: Bay of Bengal Appendix A1.1 membership
nodes.norm_label: bay of bengal appendix a1.1 membership

nodes.label: East China Sea Supplementary Table S1
nodes.rationale: Membership table is in a DOCX supplement rather than the main PDF.
nodes.norm_label: east china sea supplementary table s1

nodes.label: Ecopath group archetypes
nodes.rationale: Taxonomic, size/habitat, feeding guild, spatial strata and life-stage grouping require different mapping evidence.

nodes.label: Feeding-guild mapping requires species evidence
nodes.rationale: A family name or trophic level alone does not identify a feeding guild; the model paper member list is required.

nodes.label: Bay of Bengal spatial-stratum mapping
nodes.rationale: Maldives shelf stratum 1 lies outside LME34; strata 2 and 3 lie inside. Arbitrarily sending all coarse catch to one stratum misattributes spatial support.

nodes.label: Reject catch assigned to detritus, imports or PP groups
nodes.rationale: Basal/detrital source groups must not receive catch taxon allocations.
nodes.norm_label: reject catch assigned to detritus, imports or pp groups

nodes.label: Assembled ecopath-paper-to-ppr skill
nodes.source_location: §3 The pipeline; §7 How to run each stage
nodes.rationale: Combines extraction, taxonomy and mapping in one paper-reading workflow; assembled from source skills rather than edited directly.

nodes.label: skills/build_combined_skill.py
nodes.rationale: Current builder regenerates Claude and Codex variants plus all six archives; --check detects assembled-tree drift.

nodes.label: tools/run_sppr.py
nodes.source_location: §7 How to run each stage; §8 Traps
nodes.rationale: Safe wrapper calls run_directory directly; supports named-model runs and explicit in-place replacement.

nodes.label: Unsafe create_PPRS_excel.py shell entry point
nodes.rationale: Historical __main__ invokes full sixteen-model overwrite even for --help; never run it from a shell. Use tools/run_sppr.py and preserve the owner’s main algorithm.

nodes.label: validate_mapping.py mapping validation
nodes.source_location: §5 Measurement and member list; §7 How to run each stage
nodes.rationale: Rejects member-list contradictions and invalid catch assignments and reports coverage by confidence tier.

nodes.label: tools/build_model_workbook.py
nodes.source_location: §5 Apportionment; §7 How to run each stage

nodes.label: tools/verify_model_workbook.py
nodes.rationale: Checks model-workbook values and Excel formulas.

nodes.label: Isolated mapping comparison workflow
nodes.source_location: §7 How to run each stage; §9 Historical work in flight
nodes.rationale: make_eval_root.py and compare_mappings.py support isolated A/B comparisons; member-list backport makes the described Guinea comparison a non-inferiority test.

nodes.label: Numeric-looking failed SPPR configurations
nodes.rationale: DIVERGED, IMPLAUSIBLE, unresolved and all-zero statuses must not be mistaken for estimates. Historical examples include negative Okhotsk TE outputs and inflated Bay of Bengal sym_GE_asDC.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo regeneration variability
nodes.rationale: Historical regeneration reproduced 18 of 20 methods; MC_new_GE and MC_new_TE_EEfix vary because they sample.

nodes.label: Respect open Excel workbook locks
nodes.rationale: PermissionError and ~$ lock files require skipping/reporting rather than forcing a save.

nodes.label: Preserve external PPREstimation repositories
nodes.rationale: FishEstimation and FishEstimationAI clones belong to another project and remain intact. Historical nested gitlinks could omit files from clones.

nodes.label: Lean human-readable workbook design
nodes.rationale: Few sheets and columns are an owner requirement.

nodes.label: Superseded original handoff coverage and unfinished tasks
nodes.rationale: Historical figures and unfinished work are retained as session history, not current status. Historical 10 extracted/6 mapped/5 PPR ecosystem counts and unintegrated network map were superseded by §14.
nodes.norm_label: superseded original handoff coverage and unfinished tasks

nodes.label: Superseded Codex takeover snapshot
nodes.rationale: At takeover Guinea was still a mapping stub and Thailand/Okhotsk stage-2 files were absent; §14 explicitly supersedes these incomplete statuses.

nodes.label: Claude and Codex skill directory split
nodes.rationale: Old skills/<name> paths move under skills/claude/<name>; Codex variants are under skills/codex/<name>.
nodes.norm_label: claude and codex skill directory split

nodes.label: Completed pilot integration, 2026-09-07
nodes.rationale: Tasks 1–5 completed: Guinea mapping/comparison, source reviews, remaining usable pilot mappings, isolated new-paper validation, upstream refresh, verified atlas integration, scoped sheets, ratios and GE/TE recycling.

nodes.label: Current geographic and historical identity limitations
nodes.rationale: Thailand’s inherited 1963 filename has a 1980 payload; Okhotsk NE refers to the whole Sea; Guinea needs geographic extrapolation. These supersede incompatible earlier geographic notes.
nodes.norm_label: current geographic and historical identity limitations

nodes.label: Model coverage expansion remains separate and unstarted
nodes.rationale: Allowing existing simple calculations across known identities does not expand verified-model coverage or change the ten-ecosystem map coloring gate.
nodes.norm_label: model coverage expansion remains separate and unstarted

nodes.label: Completed annual graph view, 2026-09-07
nodes.source_location: §15 Annual graph view; §16 Site-wide carbon display
nodes.rationale: Section 15 records the completed annual feature: metrics, methods, source scopes, presets/custom sets, separate model versions, range controls and missing gaps. Owner-approved repeated 2019 NPP and matched ratios remain in force. Its 100 × sum(raw wet PPR) / 9 / sum(NPP) formula is expressed in source units; section 16 updates all site PPR masses to carbon and prohibits a second division by 9.

nodes.label: Independent raw-catch/TL and mapped-SPPR annual source checks
nodes.source_location: §15 Annual graph view; §16 Site-wide carbon display
nodes.rationale: build_time_series.py compares independently calculated annual raw-catch/TL and mapped-SPPR totals with saved workbook rows before publishing. Audited JSON and XLSX retain wet-weight PPR; browser display conversion does not alter source inputs, PPREstimation algorithms or Jensen behavior.
nodes.norm_label: independent raw-catch/tl and mapped-sppr annual source checks

nodes.label: Site-wide PPR mass display in tonnes carbon
nodes.rationale: Every PPR mass shown on the site, including map values, tooltips, legends, method-ratio component masses, annual graph axes/readouts and plotted-data CSV, uses carbon (t C). Divide source wet PPR by 9 once.
nodes.norm_label: site-wide ppr mass display in tonnes carbon

nodes.label: Audited source PPR remains wet weight
nodes.rationale: Source workbooks and audited annual input JSON retain wet-weight PPR. Presentation conversion to tonnes carbon leaves source values intact.
nodes.norm_label: audited source ppr remains wet weight

nodes.label: Non-PPR quantities retain their values
nodes.rationale: Catch stays wet weight. Recycling diagnostics and dimensionless method ratios are not converted. NPP remains in tonnes carbon and matched PPR/NPP percentages do not receive a second factor of 1/9.

nodes.label: Latest site-wide carbon display policy, 2026-09-07
nodes.rationale: The owner requested every site-displayed PPR mass in carbon. Map values/tooltips/legends, ratio component masses, graph axes/readouts and plotted-data CSV columns use tonnes carbon. This latest policy qualifies the raw-wet-unit formula recorded in section 15.

nodes.label: One browser conversion from source wet PPR to carbon
nodes.rationale: Map and annual aggregation modules divide source wet-weight PPR by 9 once. PPR/NPP is 100 × already-converted carbon PPR / NPP, with no second division. Dimensionless method ratios, recycling diagnostics, NPP and catch retain their values; source JSON/XLSX, PPREstimation algorithms and Jensen behavior are unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: one browser conversion from source wet ppr to carbon

nodes.label: Annual-feature ratio formula stated in raw source units
nodes.source_location: §15 Annual graph view; §16 Site-wide carbon display
nodes.rationale: Section 15 records 100 × sum(raw wet PPR) / 9 / sum(NPP). It is equivalent to the latest 100 × displayed carbon PPR / NPP; the source-unit formula must not cause already-converted PPR to be divided again.
nodes.norm_label: annual-feature ratio formula stated in raw source units
